summary: Six findings: two high-severity statement errors inherited from the source (unqualified classification of maps between classifying stacks and the missing properness hypothesis for a correspondence trace); four medium-severity extraction gaps concerning the scheme/diamond comparison owner, Fargues–Scholze parameter inputs, Dat's Langlands classification, and the strongly regular fixed-point theorem for buildings. All 106 missing items have exactly one route and all 25 distinct planned stage IDs resolve. The findings do not claim that the main Kottwitz theorem is false.
checked: Independence: the extraction identifies ClaudeCode session cc-442dc5 and its accepting review identifies cc-fb70e5. Codex session codex-rtOQ9t did neither job. Read both extraction deliverables, the paper review JSON and REV-PAPER-HANSEN-KALETHA-WEINSTEIN-22.md at atlas commit a97a6a4a90d113e32c44e3170064aefed84548c1.

Read on 2026-10-01 the complete mathematical text in the seven included TeX files of arXiv:1709.06651v4, including Introduction, StatementOfTheMainResult, RepresentationTheoreticPreparations, LefschetzVerdierRevised, LocalTermsOnGrassmannian, ApplicationToLocalShimuraVarieties and Appendix, together with the bibliography. The obsolete, unreferenced LefschetzVerdier.tex was not treated as the source. Downloaded the 96-page v4 PDF and source from https://arxiv.org/pdf/1709.06651v4 and https://arxiv.org/e-print/1709.06651v4.

Compared the findings with the 79-page published article, Forum of Mathematics, Pi 10 (2022), e13, DOI 10.1017/fmp.2022.7, downloaded from https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/S2050508622000075. Read the relevant published passages, including pp. 22–23, 32–33, 45, 47–49, 68–69 and 76; visually inspected pp. 22, 33 and 76 to check the formulas. This is a complete reading of the v4 mathematical TeX, with targeted comparison against the published pagination, not a claim to have reread every published page independently.

Checked all 128 extraction items, their hypotheses and locators against that reading; read all five routes, 17 prerequisites and 14 sourceIssues with their review annotations. Distinguished conditional refined-LLC results from unconditional trace-distribution results, elliptic-character equality from equality of representations, and the result after forgetting the Weil action from the full Kottwitz conjecture. The 14 already recorded source issues are not presented again as new findings.

Assembled the atlas afresh at a97a6a4 and checked route membership: 106 missing, 22 planned and no library items; every missing item occurs in exactly one route, and all 25 distinct planned stage IDs resolve. Read the relevant stage contracts and reviewed coverage for the BunG, Hecke, Satake, v-stack, excursion, adic-comparison and étale-duality owners; noted the absence of reviewed entries for some other cited stages. In particular compared AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons L1–L3 and ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction ES0, ES5, ES6 and ES7:parabolic rather than inferring their content from their titles.

Read the SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups parent and ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.2 scope, and checked fresh stage data plus proposed roadmap, packet and decomposition files for the proposed continuations and the conditional rigid-inner-form/relative-trace reuse. Did not establish a duplicate accepted owner for those continuations. Generic category, building or representation-theory prerequisites were not counted as the paper-specific theorems they support.

Searched the actual Git trees at Mathlib 082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174 and Tau Ceti f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369 for v-stacks/v-sheaves, local shtukas, Bun_G, geometric Satake, Harish-Chandra, smooth representations, nu-tempered representations, Bruhat–Tits, Lefschetz–Verdier and excursion terms. The Bruhat–Tits hit in Mathlib/Algebra/Module/Lattice.lean is an introductory lattice/tree remark; Tau Ceti's excursion hits are probabilistic/combinatorial. Read CategoryTheory.ExactPairing and HasRightDual in the pinned Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Rigid/Basic.lean: they concern ordinary monoidal categories, not the full 2-categorical cohomological-correspondence formalism. No exact endpoint was established that warrants replacing a missing item by library.

Applied PROTOCOL section 16's cited-result rule: findings 4–6 ask for definitions or supplier results explicitly used by HKW, with extraction statuses and routes. They do not require supplier proof closure, detailed Lean APIs, unit tests or formalization as conditions of completing this extraction. No Lean file is a deliverable; no build, cache download or language server was started.

Checked the publisher landing page, arXiv version history and title/erratum searches on 2026-10-01. No correction addressing findings 1–2 was found in those checks; this is a bounded search, not a claim that none exists. Source fingerprints and reproducible counterexamples are in the reader report.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-HANSEN-KALETHA-WEINSTEIN-22.result.json: item /127, route 2 and sourceIssues; companion reader report
findings.claim: Item /127 incorrectly says that all S-morphisms BG -> BH correspond to S-group homomorphisms G -> H. A map can send the trivial G-torsor to a nontrivial H-torsor on S. Thus the assertion is false for the stated arbitrary diamond S. The later formula for 2-morphisms between maps induced by specified homomorphisms does not repair this omitted torsor datum.
findings.evidence: HKW Example 4.1.1, published p. 22, says the maps 'correspond to S-homomorphisms'; the same sentence occurs in v4 LefschetzVerdierRevised.tex and is copied into /127. Take S = Spd(Q_p), G = 1 and H = the constant group Z/2 over S. An unramified quadratic extension L/Q_p gives a nontrivial H-torsor Spd(L) -> S, hence a map B1 = S -> BH. There is only one homomorphism 1 -> H, and its induced map classifies the trivial torsor. The nontrivial map is therefore not even 2-isomorphic to one induced by a homomorphism. This uses precisely the torsor interpretation of BH in the first sentence of the example.
findings.fix: Correct /127 to describe general maps by an H-torsor P on S with a G-action commuting with the right H-action (equivalently, a homomorphism G -> Aut_H(P)). Alternatively restrict the homomorphism description to maps whose value on the trivial G-torsor is trivializable, making the choice of trivialization explicit. Retain the conjugation formula for 2-morphisms between the maps induced by specified homomorphisms, without identifying that groupoid with all maps for arbitrary S. Add a sourceIssue for Example 4.1.1 under section 18 and explain this qualification in route 2/the report; it does not invalidate the later uses of maps induced by group homomorphisms. Include the quadratic-torsor example as a check on the corrected statement.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-HANSEN-KALETHA-WEINSTEIN-22.result.json: item /059, route 2 and sourceIssues; companion reader report
findings.claim: The correspondence version of /059 assumes X proper but allows arbitrary fine c:Y -> X ×_S X. It then asserts an induced endomorphism on RΓ(X,A) and integration of the trace class over Fix(c). Properness of X alone does not define either operation for an arbitrary such correspondence: the application of Theorem 4.3.8 also requires Y -> S proper, or a separately specified support condition that supplies the needed maps.
findings.evidence: Theorem 4.3.8, published p. 32, requires 'with p, q proper'. Example 4.3.10, p. 33, takes C'=S and X'=S but states only properness of X; /059 copies that omission. The required p is Y -> S. Section 5.3, p. 48, explicitly imposes properness of c_1 when constructing the cohomology operator, and properness of the relevant component when integrating a local term. For a concrete failure take X=S=Spd(C), A=Λ with Λ=F_ell and ell different from the residue characteristic, Y the countable disjoint union of S, c_1=c_2 the étale structure map and u=id_ΛY under c_2^!=c_2^*. This is an allowed fine correspondence in /051–/052. Its fixed locus is Y and its trace section is the constant sequence 1. That sequence lies in product_n Λ but not in direct-sum_n Λ, so the compact-support counit cannot integrate it; the displayed right side is undefined.
findings.fix: Add properness of Y over S to the general correspondence clause of /059, equivalently properness of c_1 in this proper-X setting, and state explicitly that this permits Theorem 4.3.8 with p:Y -> S. Preserve the automorphism case Y=X, where the condition is automatic. A more general proper-support formulation is possible only if its support data and induced operator are stated. Add a section-18 sourceIssue for Example 4.3.10, and update the report/route 2 so the false unrestricted formula is not a blueprint target. Do not describe this as a disproof of the paper's proper-correspondence applications.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-HANSEN-KALETHA-WEINSTEIN-22.result.json: item /072 planned array and route 2 imports; companion reader report
findings.claim: Item /072 assigns the characteristic-p derived comparison, including full faithfulness and compatibility with Rf_!, only to AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons:L1 and L2. Those are its construction and scheme-compactification prerequisites. The layer actually promising the comparison theorem is L3, which is omitted from both the planned array and route 2's imports.
findings.evidence: HKW section 5.3, published pp. 47–49, uses the ECD section 27 comparison and calls the derived pullback 'fully faithful'. At a97a6a4, content/campaign/AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons/README.md, L1 constructs the scheme-to-v-sheaf functor and site maps; L2 extends scheme compact support to qcqs schemes; L3 explicitly proves ECD 27.1–27.3, full faithfulness in 27.2, and the 27.4 Rf_! comparison using L2 and S0–S3. The reviewed AUDIT-18 coverage entry for L3 records these exact targets as not built. No new owner is needed.
findings.fix: Add AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons:L3 to /072's planned stages and to route 2's explicit imports, retaining L1/L2 for the constituent constructions. Explain that the actual full-faithfulness and exceptional-operation comparison is imported from L3, with the coefficient and morphism hypotheses retained. Update the report consistently; leave the existing roadmap files unchanged.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-HANSEN-KALETHA-WEINSTEIN-22.result.json: items /002–/005 and route 1; companion reader report
findings.claim: The extraction records the GL_n comparison /005 and the HKW conclusions, but has no items for the FS semisimple parameter construction, its compatibility with parabolic induction, or preservation of the parameter among irreducible cohomology constituents under the Hecke operation used here. These are explicit inputs to both removal of the error term and the inner-form GL_n comparison. Naming ES5/ES6 in a brief does not supply their statements, statuses and routes; ES6 also does not replace the specific ES7:parabolic import.
findings.evidence: HKW proof of Theorem 6.5.1, p. 68, uses equality of the parameters of every irreducible constituent of H*(i_1^* T_(V_mu^vee) i_b* rho), followed by FS Theorem I.9.6(viii), to prove supercuspidality. Section 6.6, pp. 68–69, invokes FS Proposition I.9.1 for the parameter construction and I.9.6(viii) for the reduction to supercuspidals; its final step says 'Hecke operators commute with excursion operators'. None of the 128 items states these supplier results. The fresh atlas has ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction:ES5 for the semisimple assignment and ES7:parabolic for the induction/stratum compatibility with its normalization conventions; their accepted AUDIT-20 coverage marks these as not built.
findings.fix: Add separate extraction items for the FS parameter construction, the parabolic-induction compatibility actually used, and Hecke/excursion compatibility with its consequence for the irreducible constituents of the displayed cohomology complex. Give precise coefficient, irreducibility and normalization hypotheses at the cited FS/HKW locators. Mark the first two planned at ES5 and ES7:parabolic, respectively. Check the exact ES0/Hecke/ES5 interface for the third and record it as planned where covered, or as a missing source addition to that existing owner. Explicitly import ES7:parabolic in route 1 and update its explanation. Extract the cited results; do not require a proof audit of FS.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-HANSEN-KALETHA-WEINSTEIN-22.result.json: items /123–/124 and route 3; companion reader report
findings.claim: The extraction uses ν-tempered representations and Langlands data in /123–/124 without extracting their definitions or Dat's existence/uniqueness theorem. In particular, writing π=j_P^G(σ⊗ψ) parenthetically does not record the theorem that every irreducible π has such data, nor the conditions on those data. These unnumbered paragraphs of HKW are essential to the standard-module induction proving Proposition C.2.2. Route 3 mentions the classification but its item list lacks it.
findings.evidence: Appendix C.2, published p. 76, between Lemmas C.2.3 and C.2.4, defines 'a Langlands triple': a standard Levi M, a ν-tempered irreducible σ of M(F), and an unramified ψ with -ν(ψ) in the specified positive chamber. It states uniqueness of the irreducible quotient and that every irreducible smooth representation comes from an essentially unique triple, citing Dat05 Theorem 3.11. It then defines I(π) and λ_π using that uniqueness. Items /123–/124 record the lattice consequence and the subsequent inequalities, not this supplier theorem or the definition. The SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups parent covers induction/Jacquet functors and the geometric lemma in SR.2, not Dat's ν-tempered classification.
findings.fix: Add definition items for ν-temperedness in the stated ℓ-adic valuation setting and for the Langlands triple/standard module/invariant used here, and a theorem item for Dat's classification as quoted and used on p. 76. Route the missing material once to the already proposed SmoothRepresentationsCharactersPartII (route 3); do not open a second local-representation owner. State the positive-chamber and temperedness assumptions and, in /124's Proposition C.2.5 clause, specify that μ' ranges over -ν(E(A_L,r_G^(opposite Q)(π'))) for the indicated standard parabolic Q, rather than unspecified exponents. Update the report. Supplier proof closure remains the future blueprint's work.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-HANSEN-KALETHA-WEINSTEIN-22.result.json: item /079 and route 1 imports; companion reader report
findings.claim: The extraction records Proposition 5.1.2's Grassmannian fixed-point conclusion, but omits the building fixed-point input it invokes from Tits79, 3.6.1. A general reference to the Bruhat–Tits building in /079 and the RG2.2 import is not an extraction item for that result. The generic bounded-subgroup fixed-point theorem in RG2.2 is different: it does not identify the fixed points of a strongly regular reduction element with points in its torus apartment.
findings.evidence: HKW proof of Proposition 5.1.2, published p. 45: for g in L^+T with strongly regular reduction, α(g) has nontrivial reduction for every root; Tits79, 3.6.1 is then used to conclude that the reduced-building image of a g-fixed point 'belongs to the apartment' of T. This is the step that moves a fixed Grassmannian coset into the torus apartment before the normalizer argument. No extraction item states it. At a97a6a4, ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.2 promises apartment gluing, actions, facets/fixers and a bounded-subgroup fixed-point statement, but not this stronger identification. The pinned-library searches did not find it either.
findings.fix: Add an extraction item for the precise Tits fixed-point/apartment result used in Proposition 5.1.2, retaining the valuation, split-group and root-value hypotheses from the source. Treat it as a missing source addition within the existing ReductiveGroupsPartII building direction (RG2.2, with adjacent fixer layers as needed), and make route 1 consume it. A separate building roadmap or a proof closure of Tits/BT is unnecessary. Check the other direct BT citations in the same proof while making this bounded extraction correction, assigning any additional key supplier statements their own statuses and routes.
